A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OCCAM. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on four datasets, including cost-accuracy comparisons, sampling analyses, and feature-extractor experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results on a larger classifier pool, parameter sensitivity, computational overhead, oracle performance, and classifier complementarity.

M1.justification: The nearest-neighbour estimator and variance-regularized ILP remain unchanged. v2 introduces Pareto-based classifier preselection for the large-pool experiment in A.6 and specifies an unevaluated max-min objective variant in Section 6. Algorithm 1 otherwise documents existing steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate single-label image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K. The added experiments retain these tasks and datasets; healthcare and language applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: Single Best, Random, and FrugalMCT remain in the original comparisons. Figure 14 adds an Optimal oracle comparator using true classification likelihoods. The new large-pool comparison excludes FrugalMCT after a reported five-hour noncompletion; it is not removed from the retained experiments.

E3.justification: A.6 adds a substantially different configuration: 101 candidate classifiers, with OCCAM restricted to 12 Pareto-efficient models while baselines access all 101, and costs normalized to RegNet-Y-128GF. New protocols also vary regularization and sampling parameters and evaluate oracle accuracy information. Existing benchmark splits, training settings, and defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds regularization sensitivity in Figure 4c, separate sample-size and K/s tradeoff analyses in A.7, measured overhead in A.8, an oracle-gap analysis in A.9, and classifier complementarity in A.10. These address several previously untested questions. Figure 13a largely redisplays the existing fixed-s K sweep.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetition counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The estimator-variance discussion is retained; the added K/s sweeps do not introduce run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 retain their numerical values. New Table 7 reports OCCAM accuracy drops of 0.17%, 0.37%, and 0.80% at 10%, 20%, and 40% cost reductions under the new classifier-pool setting. A.8 adds timings of 8.68 seconds for neighbour search and 15.1 seconds for ILP, alongside new sensitivity, oracle, and complementarity findings. These are additional results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The existing definitions, Lemmas 4.3-4.6, and Appendix B proofs are preserved. v2 adds the O(NsKd) nearest-neighbour complexity statement in A.8 and explicitly formulates a max-min accuracy objective in Section 6, without adding corresponding proofs.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the abstract and introduction from image classification to classification under suitable assumptions, presenting image classification as the demonstration. This is a limited scope reframing because v1 already argued generic applicability in its conclusion. The central estimator, optimal-portfolio, and 40% cost-reduction claims remain.

C2.justification: Beyond the existing well-separation discussion, v2 explicitly identifies IID/distribution-shift limitations and the shortcomings of optimizing average accuracy. It also interprets regularization stability, sampling tradeoffs, model-pool selection, overhead, and the oracle gap. A.10 explains how complementary classifiers could outperform the best individual classifier.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with a repository address, documents the 12 selected models and their costs, and supplies component timings and parameter-selection guidance. Original hardware, optimizer, splits, and temperature settings are retained; the soft-classifier implementation description moves to Appendix C.2.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions OCCAM within algorithm selection, citing Rice, and distinguishes it from mixture-of-experts routing using Shazeer and Fedus. It adds supporting application, model, and solver references while removing several historical vision citations. The main relationship to prior hybrid-inference methods remains intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and substantial introductory passages are rewritten around general classification. Related-work subsections are reordered, the combined discussion/conclusion becomes separate limitations and conclusion sections, an algorithm walkthrough is added, and implementation prose moves to Appendix C.2. These substantially reorganize the narrative despite the stable core methodology.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, Figure 4 expands from two to three panels, and Algorithm 1 adds a dedicated pseudocode display. Figures 11-15 and Tables 6-7 substantially expand the experimental presentation. Existing displays are largely retained or relocated, while Figure 13a re-expresses an earlier sampling plot.

improvement.justification: The added regularization controls, measured routing overhead, and oracle-gap analysis improve assessment of the retained method, while explicit limitations and reported code access improve transparency. However, A.6 gives OCCAM and its baselines different candidate pools and lacks a completed FrugalMCT comparison, limiting the strength of the new scalability evidence.
